label: t1-reporter-alt
summary: Keep the chosen system (threshold-steepness separability in RBS-variant Cello repressor gates) and run ONE alternative alongside it: the RBS-tuned lac-repressor induction library of Garcia & Phillips 2011 / Razo-Mejia et al. 2018 (MIT-licensed flow_master.csv, 250 KB, now on D:). I refit it myself with a 4-parameter Hill curve. Across six RBS variants (repressor copies 11 to 870 per cell), the half-maximal IPTG (EC50) moves 4.94-fold at operator O1 and 17.47-fold at O2, while the Hill coefficient stays at 1.37-1.54 (O1) and 1.46-1.69 (O2): maximum pairwise relative difference 0.116 and 0.150, and none of 15 pairs per operator has non-overlapping 95% bootstrap CIs. At the weak operator O3 the curves are too flat for n to be determined (n 0.87-1.89, CIs wide), so that case is uninformative, not supportive. This is an independent system and a different input axis (inducer, not repressor synthesis), so it supports the idea that RBS-tuned repressor level shifts the threshold without a detectable steepness change, but it does not confirm the Cello claim itself. Seven further candidates are costed in the table (Reg-Seq, Kosuri 12,563 promoter x RBS library, Marionette, Buchler-Cross yeast sequestration, Qian resource-competition cascades, EMOPEC Shine-Dalgarno library, Ozbudak translation-vs-transcription noise) plus the two the scout already had. The strongest published competing explanation is molecular titration/sequestration (Buchler & Louis 2008; Buchler & Cross 2009), which says steepness itself depends on repressor abundance and so predicts that an RBS change should change n; resource competition (Qian 2017) is the second. Two corrections to the earlier law-mapper: law set 1.8.1 no longer contains Delphi/Turing.lean or the turing-ddi-linear-condition law (replaced by candidate turing-ddi 1.1.0 with proofs in registry/proposals/turing-ddi/law.lean), and 1.8.1 still has no Hill-type or reporter law (gene-regulatory-dynamics is still a placeholder gap).
lay_summary: The main plan tests whether turning a gene's 'volume knob' (a DNA switch that sets how much repressor protein is made) shifts when a genetic switch flips without changing how sharply it flips. I looked for other experiments that could test the same idea. The best one is a long-running set of bacteria where scientists tuned how many repressor molecules each cell makes, then slowly added a chemical and watched the glow. Re-analysing their public spreadsheet, the point where the glow turned on moved five to seventeen times, yet the sharpness of the turn-on barely changed. A rival idea says the sharpness should change when the amount of repressor changes, so the main plan is a fair fight. I recommend keeping the main plan and adding this second data set as a cross-check.

findings.claim: Own Hill refit, operator O2: EC50 rises from 8.9 uM to 155.9 uM (17.47-fold, log2 4.13); n spans 1.46-1.69; max pairwise relative difference 0.150, i.e. exactly at the 0.15 bound the scout froze; 0 of 15 pairs have non-overlapping CIs.

findings.claim: In the lac data the plateau (fold change at saturating IPTG) falls as repressor copy number rises (O1 fitted plateau 1.034 at R=11 vs 0.437 at R=870), so an RBS change is NOT a pure translation of the curve along log-input here: dynamic range also changes. Cello's ymax/ymin should therefore be checked within families too.

Caveat on A1: the input axis differs from Cello gates. In the lac system RBS sets repressor copies and the input is an inducer that binds the repressor (allosteric MWC); in a Cello gate the input promoter drives repressor synthesis. So A1 tests 'RBS-tuned repressor level leaves n unchanged', not the Cello log-translation law itself.
findings.source: reasoning from paper abstracts (Razo-Mejia 2018, Nielsen 2016) and the CSV columns
findings.evidence_quote: first predicting the behavior of strains that span a large range of repressor copy numbers and DNA binding strengths and then constructing and measuring their response.

findings.claim: Garcia & Phillips 2011 used a collection of strains with a large variation in repressor copy number to test the simple-repression input-output function.
findings.evidence_quote: using the mathematical description of these regulatory motifs as a predictive tool to determine the number of repressors in a collection of strains with a large variation in repressor copy number

findings.claim: Razo-Mejia 2018 derive analytic expressions for EC50 and dynamic range from an MWC model, i.e. the thermodynamic framework gives a published number-making model for A1 (so A1 can be scored by prediction, not only descriptively).
findings.evidence_quote: enables us to derive analytic expressions for key properties such as the dynamic range and [EC50].

findings.claim: STRONGEST COMPETING EXPLANATION (1): molecular titration / sequestration generates steepness from abundance, so threshold AND steepness both depend on how much repressor/inhibitor is made; it predicts that an RBS change moves n, contrary to the chosen law. Shown experimentally in yeast with apparent Hill coefficients up to 12.
findings.evidence_quote: both the threshold and the degree of ultrasensitivity depend upon the abundance of the inhibitor, exactly as we observed experimentally.

findings.claim: Theory behind competing explanation (1): ultrasensitivity from titration is set mainly by the dissociation constant and the repressor concentration.
findings.evidence_quote: The ultrasensitive nature of the input-output response is mainly determined by two parameters: the dimer dissociation constant and the repressor concentration.

findings.claim: COMPETING EXPLANATION (2): resource competition makes gene-expression cassettes non-modular; RBS and DNA copy number change circuit shape through shared ribosomes/polymerases, so an RBS-driven shift can be a load effect.
findings.evidence_quote: These coefficients lead to nonregulatory interactions among genes that reshape the circuit's behavior.

findings.claim: COMPETING EXPLANATION (3), titration of repressor by extra binding sites: transcription-factor demand from other sites/copies changes the effective dose-response, a thermodynamic-model prediction tested experimentally.
findings.evidence_quote: we characterize the interplay between TF copy number and the demand for that TF.

findings.claim: Candidate A2, Reg-Seq (RPGroup-PBoC/RegSeq, MIT): massively parallel mutation scanning that returns binding-energy matrices; gives a mechanism-level (energy) separability test but is not a dose-response; GitHub reports repo size 324656 KB (about 317 MB), above the 150 MB cap, so NOT downloaded.
findings.source: https://api.github.com/repos/RPGroup-PBoC/RegSeq ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RPGroup-PBoC/RegSeq/master/README.md ; tree listing master (largest files 32 MB sequencing files)
findings.evidence_quote: energy matrices that characterize, in k_BT units, the binding strength of transcription factors to their target sites

findings.claim: Candidate A3, Kosuri 2013: 12,563 promoter x RBS combinations with DNA, RNA and protein read out; a ready test of whether the promoter axis and the RBS axis are separable (multiplicative) but each construct is a single state, no dose-response. The data-file location was NOT verified.
findings.evidence_quote: RNA and protein expression were within twofold of expected levels 80% and 64% of the time, respectively.

findings.claim: Kosuri 2013 also reports the failure tail of composability: the worst 5% of constructs deviated by 13-fold, which bounds how strictly any 'RBS acts independently' law can hold.
findings.evidence_quote: the worst 5% of constructs deviated from prediction by 13-fold on average

findings.claim: Candidate A4, Marionette: 12 directed-evolution-optimised sensors with >100-fold induction; useful because dose-response shape was engineered (both K and n moved by selection) - a counter-example source - but there is no RBS series. Raw data location not found.
findings.evidence_quote: a set of 12 high-performance sensors that exhibit >100-fold induction with low background and cross-reactivity.

findings.claim: Candidate A5, Buchler & Cross 2009 yeast sequestration circuit: the system in which the competing law is shown; gives a designed case where n SHOULD change with abundance (a positive control for the test's power). Values only in figures; not machine-readable here.
findings.evidence_quote: converts a graded transcriptional response into a sharply ultrasensitive response, with apparent Hill coefficients up to 12.

findings.claim: Candidate A6, Qian et al. 2017 activation-cascade library: resource demand explicitly tuned (RBS, copy number); gives the confound test (does load, not RBS, explain shifts) at the cost of building a load model; supplementary data availability not verified.
findings.evidence_quote: we create a library of genetic activation cascades in E. coli bacteria, where we explicitly tune the resource demand by each gene.

findings.claim: Candidate A7, EMOPEC (Bonde 2016): Shine-Dalgarno sequence to protein-level map; gives a validated RBS-strength predictor so 'RBS strength' becomes a number, but no dose-response. Code mirror found on GitHub (micked/EMOPEC, no licence field) but data not downloaded.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.3727 via Europe PMC; GitHub search 2026-11-12
findings.evidence_quote: Measured protein levels for 91% of our designed sequences were within twofold of the desired target level.

findings.claim: Candidate A8, Ozbudak 2002 (B. subtilis): transcription and translation rates varied independently for one reporter; gives the noise-side counter-check, since single-cell noise is NOT invariant to translation rate, which matches the scout's observation that output noise varies within a Cello family. Values in figures only.
findings.evidence_quote: increased translational efficiency is the predominant source of increased phenotypic noise.

findings.claim: Burden measurement: a capacity monitor can assay the burden imposed by constructs, so a growth/burden covariate could be read alongside any gate library to test competing explanation (2).
findings.evidence_quote: We identify construct designs with reduced burden that predictably outperformed less efficient designs, despite having equivalent output.

findings.claim: Lean implication for the track: the law to propose (as a successor of gene-regulatory-dynamics) must carry the competing explanations as named hypotheses (no titration regime; no resource coupling), because titration is the mechanism that would make n depend on abundance.

key_claims.claim: In an independent, public, RBS-tuned repressor library (lac, six RBS variants, 11 to 870 repressors per cell) my own Hill refit shows the threshold moves 4.9-fold (O1) and 17.5-fold (O2) while Hill n changes by at most 0.116 and 0.150 relative, with no pair separable at 95%; O3 is uninformative.
key_claims.evidence_quote: O2 EC50 range 8.9-155.9 uM, fold 17.47 (log2 4.13) | n range 1.46-1.69, (max-min)/mean = 0.149

key_claims.claim: The strongest published rival says steepness depends on abundance (molecular titration), so an RBS change should move n, not just K; the chosen test can therefore fail for a principled reason.
key_claims.evidence_quote: both the threshold and the degree of ultrasensitivity depend upon the abundance of the inhibitor, exactly as we observed experimentally.

key_claims.claim: The lac plateau falls with repressor copy number (O1 fitted plateau 1.03 to 0.44), so an RBS change is not a pure log-axis translation of the whole curve; Cello ymax/ymin need the same within-family check.

Law set 1.8.1 has no Hill or reporter law (gene-regulatory-dynamics still a gap) and no longer contains the Turing lemmas the earlier law-mapper cited, so any reporter law is new, not a modification of something proved.
key_claims.evidence_quote: not formalised: the map records links (expressed in, required for, sufficient for), not dynamics; the Studio may only propagate an edit to every linked node (G2)

recommendations: KEEP the chosen system. It is the only candidate where the design change (RBS in front of the repressor) acts on the same axis as the claim, with raw 250-bin histograms and untouched held-out libraries. I did not open Eco1C2G2T2 or any other holdout, so the freeze is intact.

RUN ALONGSIDE: the lac RBS library (A1) as a second, independent system. Cost: near zero (data on D:, refit takes about 2 minutes). Freeze before looking at any further operator or condition: 'n varies by at most 0.15 relative across RBS variants when curve amplitude exceeds 0.7'. Note that O2 already sits exactly at 0.150, so choose the bound and the amplitude cut-off on O1 only and score O2 and any other library as holdout; state that I have now seen both.

Add the titration model (Buchler-Louis / Buchler-Cross) as the named rival in the freeze file with its own falsifiable prediction: n increases or decreases systematically with repressor abundance within a family (trend test), versus the separability claim of no trend. The lac result is currently a mild point against a large titration effect in simple repression, not against titration in general.

Add a burden covariate (growth rate or capacity monitor, Ceroni 2015 style) to any new wet or dry leg to separate resource competition from RBS-specific effects. Cost: one extra readout per construct.
Check ymax and ymin within each Cello family, because the lac data show plateau moving with repressor level; the present freeze only tests K and n.

Low-priority extras: Kosuri 2013 for promoter-by-RBS separability (needs data-file location found first), mismatch-CRISPRi as already planned by the scout, and Reg-Seq only if a mechanistic energy-level leg is wanted (317 MB repo: fetch single files).
Lean: target the successor of gene-regulatory-dynamics at version 1.8.1; do not rely on Delphi.Turing.* names.

could_not_find: Machine-readable data for Kosuri 2013 (GEO/supplement location), Marionette, Qian 2017 and Bonde 2016: not located in this run, so those candidates are costed from abstracts only.
Buchler & Cross 2009 and Ozbudak 2002 data are in figures; I could not read values.
I did not re-fetch or recompute any Cello UCF number (including the designer's dn 0.1587 for BM3R1); those figures are the designer's. I deliberately did not open Eco1C2G2T2 or other holdouts.
I did not read Cello's fitting code, so whether the Cello fit itself constrains n remains unchecked.

The lac refit uses a plain 4-parameter Hill, not the MWC model of the paper; EC50 at high repressor counts is partly extrapolated from a curve whose plateau is below 1, and replicate rows are pooled without day effects. A sensible next step is a joint fit with n shared across RBS variants and a likelihood-ratio test; not done.
The fold-change data are bootstrapped over rows within IPTG level only (300 resamples, seed 1); CIs are therefore approximate.
The peer-reviewed version of Reg-Seq (Belliveau 2018 PNAS) was not DOI-checked; only the bioRxiv preprint DOI is cited.
The earlier law-mapper's claim that the Turing file needed a 'WellMixedStable' constraint cannot be re-checked against 1.8.1; I only verified the names are absent.
